title: Laparoscopic Peritoneal Lavage vs Laparoscopic Sigmoidectomy in Perforated Acute Diverticulitis: a Multicenter Prospective Observational Study (STELLA Study)
brief_summary: Laparoscopic peritoneal lavage (LPL) has recently been emerging as an effective alternative to laparoscopic sigmoidectomy (LS) in patients with complicated acute diverticulitis (CAD) (Modified Hinchey's classification grade II non-responder to conservative therapy and grade III). Aim of the study is to evaluate which surgical strategy, between LPL and LS, could give better results in patients with CAD
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Acute abdominal pain,
* Signs of localized or diffuse peritonitis
* Signs of suspected perforated diverticulitis (diagnostic imaging)
* Signed informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Septic shock
* Immunodepression
* Previous multiple abdominal surgical operations
* Modified Hinchey's grade IV
